basis: Gonadal dysgenesis and impaired gonadal hormone function characterize the major sex chromosome DSD subtypes; other organ defects vary across subtypes.
Alloimmune sensitization against red-cell Rh antigens defines this blood-group incompatibility; fetal complications are not assumed.
Intrahepatic portal venous sclerosis defines disease; anemia 80-99% and hypersplenism/leukopenia 30-79% support blood-organ involvement. Varices are vascular.
Developmental impairment and cardiac anomalies define syndrome; strabismus 30-79% and clinodactyly 7/15 support eye and skeletal involvement. Ear shape alone does not establish dysfunction.
Defining blepharoptosis affects eyelids, cleft palate and dental anomalies affect the oral apparatus, and ectrodactyly affects the skeleton.
Rickettsial spotted-fever infection; transient rash does not establish skin damage, and common lasting injury to another organ is not established.
Inherited pyrophosphate metabolism defect causes generalized arterial calcification and cardiac injury. Nephrocalcinosis and hypophosphatemic rickets occur in only 5-29%.
Malignant glial tumor originates in the spinal cord and invades neural tissue; weakness and incontinence reflect neurologic injury.
Cardiac, skeletal and skin findings define MASS; myopia is a characteristic defining ocular manifestation. Dural ectasia without neural dysfunction does not establish neurologic damage.
Ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor of hormone-producing gonadal cells; estrogenic or androgenic manifestations establish its endocrine role.
Inherited high myopia is an ocular growth and refractive disorder; associated retinal holes and cataracts remain within the ocular axis.
Benign ossifying tumor originates in the ocular choroid; its bone composition does not establish skeletal-system disease.
Thrombosis occupies mesenteric veins. Gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish common bowel injury; intestinal infarction is not demonstrated in at least 30%.
Graphite dust causes pneumoconiosis and pulmonary fibrosis; the defining injury is in lung tissue.
Childhood interstitial lung disease defines pulmonary injury; extrapulmonary manifestations depend on the underlying subtype.
CoQ-responsive oxidative phosphorylation deficiency is an energy-metabolism disorder; supplied information does not establish the frequency of injury to specific organs.
Developmental delay and intellectual impairment are common across partial trisomy 8 syndromes; other organ malformations vary with the duplicated segment.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy directly affects brain function; seizures and absent speech occur in 4/4 patients. Hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.
Mitochondrial defect with cardiomyopathy; myopathy supported by weakness 1/2 and muscle atrophy/biopsy changes 1/1; intellectual disability 1/1. Cataract 1/1 omitted by cap; sparse data.
Hereditary malformations of the anus and rectum, including anal atresia and rectovaginal fistula, define gastrointestinal involvement.
Primary epiphyseal bone dysplasia causes joint abnormalities and degeneration; rare myopathy remains within the same axis. No common extraskeletal injury is established.
Partial opacification of the ocular lens defines immature cataract.
Mixed sclerosing bone dystrophy and increased bone density establish skeletal disease; unspecified extraskeletal manifestations cannot support additional organs or frequencies.
Inherited alkaline-phosphatase deficiency impairs skeletal mineralization; prenatal limb shortening and bowing define this form. Later manifestations are not assumed.
Developmental proximal femoral epiphyseal disease causes femoral-head necrosis, cystic changes or sclerosis; other collagenopathy manifestations are not established for this group.
